items.title: Trump Backs a 10% Card Rate Cap With Democrats. That’s a Big Risk for JPMorgan and Citigroup
items.summary: Key TakeawaysPresident Trump said Saturday he would cap credit card interest rates at 10%, against a median card rate of about 22. 2%.

items.title: Big Short Investor Steve Eisman: Banks Are “Safer Today Than at Any Point in My Career.” Good News for Citigroup
items.summary: Key TakeawaysSteve Eisman says reckless mortgage lending inside banks is less of a risk than at any point in his career, and puts Citigroup’s leverage at 10 to 1, down from about 40 to 1. The past week’s scares came from technology: a JPMorgan outage and a Fed warning that AI agents could speed up bank runs.

items.title: Citi Just Cut Its Alibaba Target to $160. Could the Stock Really Climb 97%?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCiti cut its Alibaba price target to $160 from $193 on Nov. 20 and kept its Buy rating, a day after a September-quarter report in which adjusted earnings missed estimates.

items.title: Renaissance Technologies Opened $739 Million in New Positions in Three Big Banks
items.summary: The quant giant behind the Medallion Fund just piled into three Wall Street heavyweights, then watched those stocks tumble within days of the filing. Does a 13F snapshot reveal conviction, or only a moment already gone?

items.title: Does Citigroup (C) Risk Error And USDC Pilot Change The Investment Case?
items.summary: Citigroup (NYSE:C) identified a US$35b risk modeling error in its European trading unit’s risk weighted asset calculations in 2026. The bank reported that the discrepancy was found through internal reviews and said it moved to adjust its models and capital metrics. Citigroup and partners ran a pilot using USDC stablecoins for cross border World Bank development disbursements to test on chain settlement. Focusing only on the US$35b risk modeling error and USDC pilot misses how these shifts...

items.title: Citi Undercounted $35 Billion in Assets at U.K. Subsidiary
items.summary: The record-keeping blunder, which was related to risk-weighted assets, is a setback for CEO Jane Fraser’s efforts to strengthen internal controls.

items.title: Citi Forced To Inject Capital After Underestimating Risky Assets By $35 Billion
items.summary: The error involved an unauthorized internal model at Citigroup's British securities unit, which said the subsidiary remained compliant with minimum regulatory requirements.

items.title: 4 Wall Street Giants That Raised Their Dividends for Income Investors
items.summary: Four big banks keep lifting their payouts, yet each one hides a different threat to the next raise. One cut its dividend to a dime, and another sits on a capital cushion that is shrinking fast. Which check can retirees trust most?
